title: Lévy distance bound from smooth test functions
statement: Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer and let $mu,nu$ be probability measures on $bbr$. Define their Lévy distance as the infimum of all $deltage0$ such that, for every $uinbbr$, $(nu((-infty,u-delta]).toReal-delta)lemu((-infty,u]).toReal$ and $mu((-infty,u]).toReallenu((-infty,u+delta]).toReal+delta$. Suppose $Bge0$ and, for every $(m+1)$ times continuously differentiable function $phi:bbrtobbr$, every $Cge0$ bounding $|phi^{(m+1)}(t)|$ for all $t$, the difference of its integrals against $mu$ and $nu$ has absolute value at most $CB$. Then for every $eta>0$, the Lévy distance is at most $(m+2)eta+(2^m/eta^{m+1})B$.
